chunks: 4 - My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn Amer, from Ahmad ibn Rizq al-Ghamshani, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala', from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

A servant remained in the Fire for seventy autumns, and each autumn is seventy years. He said: Then he asked God, Mighty and Majestic: "By the right of Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, why have You not shown mercy to me?"

He said: So God, Exalted is His Majesty, revealed to Gabriel: "Descend to My servant and remove him." He said: "O Lord, how can I descend into the Fire?" He said: "I have commanded it to be cool and peaceful for you." He said: "O Lord, I do not know where he is." So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "He is in a pit in Sijjin." He said: So he descended into the Fire and found him chained upon his face, and took him out.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "O My servant, how long were you calling upon Me in the Fire?" He said: "I cannot count it, O my Lord." He said: "By My glory! Had you not asked Me by it, I would have prolonged your torment in the Fire. But I have decreed upon Myself that no servant shall ask Me by the right of Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt except that I will forgive him for what was between Me and him. And I have forgiven you today."

key_terms.حتمت على نفسي: I have decreed upon Myself; a divine self-imposed obligation expressing God's mercy
key_terms.خريف: autumn; used here as a unit of time equal to seventy years in the Hereafter
key_terms.سجين: Sijjin; the lowest depths of Hell or a register of deeds for the wicked (cf. Quran 83:7-9)

ai.seo_question: What does Islamic tradition say about seeking intercession through the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Baqir (AS) in a teaching assembly recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in 368 AH, conveys that a sinner who spent an unimaginably long time in hellfire was ultimately saved when he supplicated to God by invoking the right of Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt. God then declared a universal divine decree that any servant who calls upon Him through this intercession will be forgiven. The narrative emphasizes the immense intercessory power and special station of the Prophet and his household, a central tenet of Shia theology that the original audience — students of hadith in Qum — would have understood as affirming the doctrines of tawassul (seeking means of approach to God) and shafa'a (intercession).

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhamad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. `Imran al-Ash`ari narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Kufi from al-`Abbas b. `Amer from Ahmad b. Rizq al-Ghamshani from Yahya b. Abi'l `Ala’ from Jabir from Abi Ja`far (as). He said:

A worshiper will spend seventy winters in the Fire, and each winter will be equivalent to seventy years. He said: Then, he will ask Allah: “By the right of Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, why did You not have mercy on me?”

He said: So, Allah will reveal to Gabriel: “Descend to My worshiper and remove him.” He will say: “O Lord! How will I descend into the Fire?” He will say: “I have commanded it to be cool and peaceful for you.” He will say: “O Lord! I do not know where he is.” So, He will say: “He is in a pit in Sijjin.” He said: So, he will descend into the Fire, and find him chained up and upon his face. He will take him out.

So, He will say: “O My servant! How long did you call for Me in the Fire?” He said: “I cannot comprehend it, my Lord.” He will say: “By My glory! Had you not asked, I would have prolonged your torment in the Fire. However, I have written upon Myself that no worshiper shall ask Me by the right of Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt except that I will forgive him for what is between him and I. So, I have forgiven you today.”
